context_requirements: Active fatty acid synthesis (FASN expression and acetyl-CoA/malonyl-CoA supply)
Dependence on de novo lipogenesis rather than exogenous lipid uptake
Intact lipogenic transcriptional feedback (SREBP-1/INSIG1 axis) for the compensatory sterol/lipid gene response
Cellular capacity to mount an integrated stress response / UPR under lipid stress
falsifiers: No decrease in FASN or other lipogenic enzyme transcripts at 6 h or 24 h in any line
No compensatory up-regulation of cholesterol synthesis genes (HMGCR, HMGCS1, INSIG1, FDFT1) at 6 h
No late (24 h) proliferation_down or G1 arrest signature in FASN-dependent lines such as HT29, MCF7, PC3, VCAP
Strong and equal transcriptional responses in all nine lines including non-lipogenic HA1E
Predominant interferon or heat-shock signature rather than lipid-metabolic and stress signatures

evidence.supports: FASN inhibitors reduce melanoma metastasis and angiogenesis, consistent with anti-proliferative and anti-angiogenic consequences of FASN inhibition
FASN inhibitors including triclosan, C75 and orlistat induce distinct changes in cell cycle, lipid content and expression of key lipid metabolism enzymes in prostate cancer cells
Orlistat inhibits FASN and reduces growth and metastasis of oral squamous cell carcinoma, supporting FASN dependence in epithelial tumors
Cerulenin induces apoptosis in colorectal cancer cells and reduces liver metastasis, with reduced phospho-Akt, linking FASN inhibition to apoptosis and PI3K/Akt signaling
Orlistat causes G1 cell cycle arrest and caspase-3-mediated apoptosis in HT-29 colorectal carcinoma, supporting G1 arrest and apoptosis as downstream effects
